generator.params.short_share.why: A devil's club stem bears its huge leaves only in a tuft at its top, round the year's growth and the flowers, and none along the bare, prickly stem below (Wikipedia's photograph: large leaves on the top of stems), so no bud behind the tip grows a leafy short shoot.

generator.params.long_share.why: Its stems are sparsely branched (FEIS, Howard 1993): a stem grows on from its tip year after year and forks only where it has flowered, not into a spreading crown of side shoots.

generator.params.terminal_bloom.why: Its flower clusters end the stems (a terminal panicle or raceme of umbels, Flora of China's Oplopanax) every year a stem is old enough to flower.

generator.params.bloom_shoots.why: A sparsely branched stem (FEIS, Howard 1993) grows on after flowering from the one bud below its cluster, not forking into two, so it flowers year after year and stays a single stem.

generator.params.sucker_lean.why: Its stems stand erect to slightly spreading (FEIS, Howard 1993), the outer ones of a clump leaning out farther than a shrub's usual 15 degrees, as the clump's stems do where they rise from layered and sprouting bases.

generator.params.pipe_tip.why: Its few stems are stout for their height, thick as a walking stick (its other name, devil's walking stick), as Corner's rules tie large leaves to thick, little-branched axes; each tip about 8 mm thick is ours, by eye from photographs, until a flora measures the stems.

traits.rosette.note: Wikipedia, Devil's club (read 2026-10-19): its photograph of the plant's form is captioned 'large leaves on the top of stems'; the leaves spirally arranged on the stems, 20-40 cm across (citing Pojar and MacKinnon 1994).

rules.note: FEIS's devilsclub review (Howard 1993, read 2026-10-19): an erect to slightly spreading deciduous shrub 1-3 m tall, sparsely branched, with sharp dense prickles on the stems; it reproduces by rhizomes and/or layering and may sprout from the root crown. Wikipedia, Devil's club (read 2026-10-19): large leaves on the top of stems. The stems' 8 mm tip thickness is ours, by eye. Flora of China vol. 13 (2007), Oplopanax (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs armed with numerous prickles; the inflorescence a terminal panicle or raceme of umbels.
